text:
jia: Heads up — saw a strange spike in the cost card for canary routing. Cache savings are showing up under model:default instead of route:signup-flow. @sam @mike can you take a look? Screenshot attached (will paste shortly).

sam: ack. can you paste the query/trace that produced the card? wondering if this is a telemetry join problem or a rendering bug.

jia: pasted the console stacktrace and a quick query we used to sanity-check:
```
SELECT route_id, model_sku, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(cache_saved_tokens) as cache_saved
FROM token_events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1 day'
GROUP BY route_id, model_sku
ORDER BY cache_saved DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
The raw rows show route_id='signup-flow' with cache_saved=420k but the dashboard shows the savings rolled into model_sku='default' without route breakdown.

mike: hmm. router attaches billing metadata at ingress via `billing_context` header. If the sidecar or router bubbles up `model_tag` but drops `route_tag` during canonicalization we'll lose the route attribute during aggregation. I think the aggregator is grouping by model_sku first then attributing cache credits to the first-seen key.

alexa: from the console POV, this manifests as a single-row savings card with no drilldown link. UX question: should the cost card show both 'raw savings' and 'attributed savings' columns? i.e., raw=cache tokens observed, attributed=disambiguated across route/model by our heuristics. That would make anomalies clearer.

ops-bot: deploy-prod Canary rollout started by @deploybot at 2024-10-04T12:34:10Z :rocket:

sam: mike, can you confirm where in the pipeline route_id could get lost? My guess is the pre-aggregation mapper (`event-normalizer`) flattens `billing_context` to a `billing_key` and we treat it as scalar.

mike: yep. quick diff I sketched:
```
- billing_key = billing_context.get('model_sku')
+ billing_key = (billing_context.get('route_id') or billing_context.get('model_sku'))
```
That would prefer route attribution when available and keep fallback to model. Also we should emit `route_id` into token_ledger for future queries.

alexa: if we change that we need to think about rollout UX: historical data will be split differently. propose feature flag `show_per_route_breakdown` (off by default) and a migration that backfills route attribution for last 7 days so dashboard parity is maintained.

jia: agreed. I'll open a small PR to prefer route_id in normalizer and add a feature flag to the console. Also adding a note in the cost-card tooltip: "attribution may change during rollout".

sam: add unit test that simulates two events with identical model_sku but different route_id and ensure aggregator splits cache savings. Also add an integration check that verifies console shows both columns when flag true.

mike: we've got to be careful about high-cardinality routes. maybe cap the per-route breakdown to top-N routes and aggregate the rest under "other". That keeps the card stable.

alexa: good call. UI will show top 5 routes by savings + "other". Also will surface a tiny latency note: "per-route attribution may increase query latency ~10-15ms when enabled" so folks aren't surprised.

jia: filing PR and linking TODOs in thread. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2141 (WIP)

sam: thx. once the PR is up ping me and I'll add the test harness. we should also add a short doc blurb in the console changelog.

mike: I'll prep a migration that adds `effective_route` to token_ledger and backfills using recent traces. plan: backfill async with safe window.

alexa: will mock the UI and post screenshots in the PR for product review.

jia: closing loop — will enable feature flag in staging after PR lands, then run a canary for 24h to confirm no large cost regressions. :+1:
